newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ING launches Romania life insurance project.
newsitem.headline: ING launches Romania life insurance project.

text.p: Dutch financial services firm ING Groep NV said on Tuesday it had launched life insurance products in Romania, in a move to strenghten its position in the region and the Balkan country.

The new insurer Nederlanden Asigurari de Viata Romania SA (NAVR) said in a statement it offered five life insurance products tailored to the requirements of the local market and to the Romanians' "various financial possibilities."
The group is the first to launch Western-type products into the Romanian life insurance market.

The statement said the NAVR's official inauguration would take place in September after the new company, which started its operation through five local offices across the country, would evaluate its first three months of activity.
"I think our evolution in Romania will be extremely interesting," said NAVR General Manager Jetse de Vries.
ING had "carefully studied and analysed" the local market for two years before launching the NAVR, the statement said.
ING would implement its tried-and-tested greenfield strategy, recruiting and training a local tied agency force for the project, company sources said.

Post-communist Romania offers attractive prospects for the insurance industry and it is just beginning to wake up to the idea that an effective and forward-looking insurance sector is essential for successful business.
Romania, where the insurance market is still dominated by state-run insurance companies, so far has done little by way of safety nets for individual and companies.
The new centrist government, which ousted leftists in elections last November, is trying to push through new legislation to strenghten the country's insurance facilities.
The new bill is expected to bolster regulatory powers and increase the cover available from private insurers. It will also raise minimum capital requirements, now at around $4000.
ING, which already has a banking operation in Romania, is also present in Eastern Europe in Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic.
